long_biography.plain_text:
The Perfetti family's confectionery enterprise began near Milan with simple sweets and chewing gum, later gaining mass recognition through Brooklyn. Giorgio Perfetti and his brother Augusto inherited the business from founder Ambrogio Perfetti and their uncle Egidio after the older generation died in the late 1980s.

The brothers pursued international expansion rather than merely preserving the inherited company. Perfetti acquired the remaining shares of Dutch confectioner Van Melle in 2001 and bought Chupa Chups in 2006, adding Mentos, Fruittella and the lollipop brand to the portfolio. Giorgio is no longer part of day-to-day management. Executive responsibility now sits with professional managers and next-generation family members. His durable relationship is that of an inheriting family shareholder whose wealth remains tied to the private candy and gum group.

uncertainties.detail: The source record's 11 August 1946 date is publicly documented for Augusto Perfetti. It should not be retained as verified Giorgio data. Forbes listed Giorgio as 59 in 2026, while older Swiss reporting described him as about 70 in 2017; no authoritative exact Giorgio birth date resolved the conflict. The dossier therefore proposes no replacement birth field and recommends manual removal or quarantine of the existing date.

The existing https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Perfetti URL now redirects to the Perfetti Van Melle company article rather than a dedicated person page. It should not be treated as a verified person social, but no social-removal operation is proposed in this research-only dossier.

Current Forbes and independent reporting identify Giorgio and Augusto as owners or controllers of the private group. Reliable reviewed sources do not disclose Giorgio's exact current personal percentage, and newer reporting points to a leadership transition within the family. The dossier accepts co-ownership without assuming a 50% stake.

Giorgio helped expand the inherited company but has not held an evidenced day-to-day management role for years. Current sources identify Sameer Suneja as CEO and Egidio and Daniele Perfetti in chair roles; these responsibilities and the company's operating assets cannot be attributed to Giorgio.

Perfetti Van Melle and its holding companies own the brands, factories, subsidiaries, cash and operating assets. Group revenue, profit, cash flow, transaction values and aggregate family wealth estimates establish scale but are not Giorgio's personal assets or net worth.

Forbes maintained a current Giorgio person profile in 2026, and recent Swiss reporting continued to identify him as a controlling family member. No reliable death report was found, so the record's living status remains supported.
No verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website met the acceptance threshold. Only the exact Forbes profile and official company-history page are proposed.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, irrelevant private-family detail and all private-vessel and collectible-asset research were excluded. None contributes to the identity, classification or biography claims.
